messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Quizzy runs quizzes during conference talks. A moderator shows the questions on the big screen, and the audience answers on their phones. The first release covers the moderator's side: preparing quizzes.

The design is in `docs/mockups/`, exported from our design tool: a style guide and two screens of this release (the quiz page and the question form), each as a static HTML page (open it in a browser) and a PNG. The stylesheet and the font next to them are the design's assets: use them as they are or adapt them. Follow the look: colors, typography, pill buttons, and layout. Big-screen pages run on LED walls and projectors; player pages run on phones.

The moderator area lives under `/moderate`. Every page in it requires HTTP Basic authentication with the credentials from `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`. Missing or wrong credentials get `401`.

Quizzes:

- `/moderate` lists the quizzes and has the "New quiz" button.
- The quiz form has one field, "Title" (required), and the "Save quiz" button. Saving opens the quiz page.
- The quiz page shows the title and the questions in order. It has the "Add question" button, the "Settings" link and the "Preview" link.
- "Settings" opens the same quiz form for the quiz, and the "Delete quiz" button, which asks for confirmation.

Questions are single-choice with text options. The question form has:

- "Question": the question text (required)
- option rows: each row has a text field labelled "Option 1", "Option 2", and so on, and a checkbox labelled "Option 1 is correct", "Option 2 is correct", and so on. A new question starts with four empty rows. The "Add option" button adds one more row with the next number.
- "Active": a checkbox, on by default
- the "Save question" button

Rules for options:

- Empty rows are skipped.
- A question needs at least two options. Otherwise the form shows "Add at least two options".
- At least one option must be correct (several correct options are fine). Otherwise the form shows "Mark at least one option as correct".
- When a rule fails, nothing is saved and the form keeps what the moderator typed.

Each question on the quiz page shows its text and its options, with the correct options marked. It also has:

- "Move up" and "Move down" buttons that change the order
- the "Active" checkbox: changing it saves at once, with no extra button
- the "Edit" link to the question form
- the "Delete" button, which asks for confirmation

Inactive questions stay on the quiz page, but the preview skips them.

The preview lets the moderator try the quiz as a player would. It goes through the active questions in order, one at a time:

- It shows the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options as buttons.
- Picking an option shows "Correct!" or "Wrong!" and reveals the correct options.
- The "Next question" button opens the next question. After the last question, the "See score" button shows the result, for example "Score: 2/3".
- The "Start over" button restarts the preview. Preview answers are not stored anywhere.

require "propshaft/compiler"

class Propshaft::Compiler::CssAssetUrls < Propshaft::Compiler
  ASSET_URL_PATTERN = /url\(\s*["']?(?!(?:\#|%23|data:|http:|https:|\/\/))([^"'\s?#)]+)([#?][^"')]+)?\s*["']?\)/

  def compile(asset, input)
    input.gsub(ASSET_URL_PATTERN) { asset_url resolve_path(asset.logical_path.dirname, $1), asset.logical_path, $2, $1 }
  end

  def referenced_by(asset, references: Set.new)
    asset.content.scan(ASSET_URL_PATTERN).each do |referenced_asset_url, _|
      referenced_asset = load_path.find(resolve_path(asset.logical_path.dirname, referenced_asset_url))

      if referenced_asset && references.exclude?(referenced_asset)
        references << referenced_asset
        references.merge referenced_by(referenced_asset, references: references)
      end
    end

    references
  end

  private
    def resolve_path(directory, filename)
      if filename.start_with?("../")
        Pathname.new(directory + filename).relative_path_from("").to_s
      elsif filename.start_with?("/")
        filename.delete_prefix("/").to_s
      else
        (directory + filename.delete_prefix("./")).to_s
      end
    end

    def asset_url(resolved_path, logical_path, fingerprint, pattern)
      if asset = load_path.find(resolved_path)
        %[url("#{url_prefix}/#{asset.digested_path}#{fingerprint}")]
      else
        Propshaft.logger.warn "Unable to resolve '#{pattern}' for missing asset '#{resolved_path}' in #{logical_path}"
        %[url("#{pattern}")]
      end
    end
end

# A single-choice question with text options.
#
# Options are edited as "rows" (see #option_rows=). Rows with blank text are
# skipped. A question needs at least two options and at least one of them must
# be correct. Rules are checked before anything is written; the options are
# replaced in the same transaction as the question.
class Question < ApplicationRecord
  MIN_OPTIONS = 2
  FORM_OPTION_ROWS = 4

  belongs_to :quiz, inverse_of: :questions
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  validates :text, presence: true
  validate :validate_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  before_create :place_at_end
  after_save :save_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  # Rows as typed in the form: [{ text:, correct: }, ...], in display order.
  # Assigning rows does not touch the database until the question is saved.
  def option_rows=(rows)
    @option_rows = Array(rows).map do |row|
      { text: row[:text].to_s, correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) == true }
    end
  end

  def option_rows
    @option_rows
  end

  # Rows to show in the form: what was typed, or the saved options, padded to
  # FORM_OPTION_ROWS so the form always has room for new options.
  def form_option_rows
    rows = @option_rows || options.map { |option| { text: option.text, correct: option.correct } }
    rows + Array.new([ FORM_OPTION_ROWS - rows.size, 0 ].max) { { text: "", correct: false } }
  end

  def move_up
    move_by(-1)
  end

  def move_down
    move_by(1)
  end

  private

  def kept_option_rows
    (@option_rows || []).select { |row| row[:text].strip.present? }
  end

  def validate_option_rows
    kept = kept_option_rows
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if kept.size < MIN_OPTIONS
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if kept.none? { |row| row[:correct] }
  end

  def save_option_rows
    Option.where(question_id: id).delete_all
    kept_option_rows.each.with_index(1) do |row, position|
      Option.create!(question: self, text: row[:text].strip, correct: row[:correct], position: position)
    end
    @option_rows = nil
    options.reset
  end

  def place_at_end
    self.position = quiz.questions.maximum(:position).to_i + 1
  end

  def move_by(step)
    ordered = quiz.questions.reorder(:position, :id).to_a
    index = ordered.index { |question| question.id == id }
    target = index && index + step
    return if index.nil? || target.negative? || target >= ordered.size

    ordered[index], ordered[target] = ordered[target], ordered[index]
    Question.transaction do
      ordered.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        question.update_column(:position, position) unless question.position == position
      end
    end
    reload
  end
end

# One "play it as a player" run through a quiz's active questions.
#
# Nothing is stored: the whole run travels in the URL. `results` holds one
# character per answered question ("1" correct, "0" wrong), and `pick` is the
# option chosen for the question on screen, if any.
class QuizPreview
  attr_reader :questions

  def initialize(questions, results: nil, pick: nil)
    @questions = questions.to_a
    @results = results.to_s.delete("^01")[0, @questions.size]
    @pick = pick.to_s
  end

  def total
    questions.size
  end

  def empty?
    questions.empty?
  end

  def answered
    @results.length
  end

  def results
    @results
  end

  def finished?
    !empty? && answered >= total
  end

  def score
    @results.count("1")
  end

  def current_question
    questions[answered] unless empty? || finished?
  end

  def last_question?
    answered + 1 == total
  end

  def picked_option
    return unless current_question && @pick.present?

    current_question.options.find { |option| option.id.to_s == @pick }
  end

  def revealed?
    picked_option.present?
  end

  def correct_pick?
    picked_option&.correct? || false
  end

  # The results string once the question on screen is answered.
  def results_with_answer
    @results + (correct_pick? ? "1" : "0")
  end
end

module Moderate
  # Everything under /moderate needs the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.
  class BaseController < ApplicationController
    layout "moderator"

    # Runs before the CSRF check, so anonymous requests always get a 401.
    prepend_before_action :require_moderator

    private

    def require_moderator
      authenticate_or_request_with_http_basic("Quizzy moderator") do |username, password|
        moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      end
    end

    def moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      expected_username = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"].to_s
      expected_password = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"].to_s
      return false if expected_username.empty? || expected_password.empty?

      ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(username.to_s, expected_username) &&
        ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(password.to_s, expected_password)
    end
  end
end

messages.content: Now `bin/serve`. It checks the required variables, makes sure gems resolve from the local installation, runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, then runs Rails in the foreground on all interfaces.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > bin/serve <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quizzy: prepare the app and run it in production mode, in the foreground.
#
#   RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
#   QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve
#
# Everything the app needs lives under storage/ (SQLite databases) and
# public/assets (precompiled files). Nothing here talks to external services.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

for name in SECRET_KEY_BASE QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD; do
  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
    echo "bin/serve: $name must be set" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Gems come from the local installation; resolving them must not need the network.
bundle check >/dev/null 2>&1 || bundle install --local

mkdir -p storage tmp/pids log
rm -f tmp/pids/server.pid

bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails assets:precompile

exec bin/rails server --environment "$RAILS_ENV" --binding 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" --pid tmp/pids/server.pid
EOF
chmod +x bin/serve && bash -n bin/serve && echo syntax-ok && cat .gitignore | tail -3 && printf '\n# Local secrets and credentials are supplied through environment variables.\n/config/master.key\n' >> .gitignore && cat .github/workflows/ci.yml | head -60

require "test_helper"

# Browser tests drive the system Chromium through Cuprite (no Selenium, no network).
class ApplicationSystemTestCase < ActionDispatch::SystemTestCase
  driven_by :cuprite, screen_size: [ 1280, 1000 ], options: {
    browser_path: ENV.fetch("BROWSER_PATH", "/usr/bin/chromium"),
    headless: true,
    process_timeout: 60,
    timeout: 15,
    browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil, "disable-dev-shm-usage" => nil }
  }

  setup do
    # Every /moderate page asks for HTTP Basic credentials; answer them for the browser.
    page.driver.browser.network.authorize(user: ActiveSupport::TestCase::MODERATOR_USER,
                                          password: ActiveSupport::TestCase::MODERATOR_PASSWORD) do |request|
      request.continue
    end
  end
end

class QuizPreparationTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  QUESTION_TEXT = "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?".freeze

  test "create a quiz, see it on its page, and open its settings" do
    visit "/moderate"
    click_button "New quiz"
    fill_in "Title", with: "Frontend Fest 2026"
    click_button "Save quiz"

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Frontend Fest 2026"
    assert_text "No questions yet"
    assert_link "Settings"
    assert_link "Preview"
    assert_button "Add question"

    click_link "Settings"
    assert_field "Title", with: "Frontend Fest 2026"
    fill_in "Title", with: "Frontend Fest 2027"
    click_button "Save quiz"
    assert_selector "h1", text: "Frontend Fest 2027"
  end

  test "a blank title is refused and the form keeps what was typed" do
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/new"
    click_button "Save quiz"
    assert_text "Title can't be blank"
    assert_current_path "/moderate/quizzes"
  end

  test "a new question starts with four empty option rows, all of them active" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}/questions/new"
    assert_checked_field "Active"

      assert_field "Option #{number}", with: ""
      assert_unchecked_field "Option #{number} is correct"
    end
    assert_no_selector "input[name='question[options][4][text]']"
  end

  test "add option appends the next numbered row" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}/questions/new"
    click_button "Add option"
    assert_field "Option 5", with: ""
    assert_unchecked_field "Option 5 is correct"
  end

    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}"
    click_button "Add question"

    fill_in "Question", with: QUESTION_TEXT
    fill_in "Option 1", with: "418"
    fill_in "Option 2", with: "429"
    check "Option 2 is correct"
    fill_in "Option 3", with: "503"
    click_button "Save question"

    assert_current_path "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}", ignore_query: true
    within(".question-item", text: QUESTION_TEXT) do
      assert_selector ".question-item__options li", count: 3
      assert_selector ".question-item__options li.is-correct", text: "429"
      assert_text "A. 418"
      assert_text "B. 429"
    end
  end

  test "option rows are skipped when empty and the typed values survive a rule failure" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}/questions/new"
    fill_in "Question", with: "Typed question"
    fill_in "Option 1", with: "Only one"
    check "Option 1 is correct"
    click_button "Save question"

    assert_text "Add at least two options"
    assert_field "Question", with: "Typed question"
    assert_field "Option 1", with: "Only one"
    assert_checked_field "Option 1 is correct"
    assert_equal 0, quiz.questions.count

    fill_in "Option 2", with: "Second"
    click_button "Save question"
    assert_text "Mark at least one option as correct"
    assert_field "Option 2", with: "Second"
    assert_equal 0, quiz.questions.count

    check "Option 2 is correct"
    click_button "Save question"
    assert_selector ".question-item", text: "Typed question"
    assert_equal 2, quiz.questions.first.options.count
    assert_equal %w[Only\ one Second], quiz.questions.first.options.map(&:text)
  end

    assert_equal [ "First question", "Second question" ], question_texts

    within(".question-item", text: "Second question") { click_button "Move up" }
    assert_equal [ "Second question", "First question" ], question_texts

    within(".question-item", text: "Second question") { click_button "Move down" }
    assert_equal [ "First question", "Second question" ], question_texts
    assert first.reload.position < Question.find_by!(text: "Second question").position

    within(".question-item", text: "Switch me") { uncheck "Active" }

require "test_helper"

class QuestionTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
  end

  test "a question needs text" do
    question = @quiz.questions.new(active: true)
    question.option_rows = rows([ [ "A", true ], [ "B", false ] ])
    assert_not question.save
    assert_includes question.errors.full_messages, "Question can't be blank"
  end

  test "a question needs at least two options" do
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "Only", true ] ]))
    assert_not question.save
    assert_equal [ "Add at least two options" ], question.errors.full_messages
  end

  test "at least one option must be correct" do
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "A", false ], [ "B", false ] ]))
    assert_not question.save
    assert_equal [ "Mark at least one option as correct" ], question.errors.full_messages
  end

  test "both rules are reported together" do
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "A", false ] ]))
    assert_not question.save
    assert_equal [ "Add at least two options", "Mark at least one option as correct" ], question.errors.full_messages
  end

  test "blank rows are skipped, including ones marked correct" do
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "", true ], [ "  ", false ], [ "A", true ], [ "", false ], [ "B", false ] ]))
    assert question.save, question.errors.full_messages.inspect
    assert_equal %w[A B], question.options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ true, false ], question.options.map(&:correct)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], question.options.map(&:position)
  end

  test "several correct options are fine" do
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "A", true ], [ "B", true ] ]))
    assert question.save
    assert_equal 2, question.options.count(&:correct)
  end

  test "a rule failure saves nothing and keeps the typed rows" do
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "Keep me", true ], [ "", false ] ]))
    assert_no_difference [ "Question.count", "Option.count" ] do
      assert_not question.save
    end
    assert_equal [ "Keep me", "" ], question.form_option_rows.first(2).map { |row| row[:text] }
  end

  test "editing replaces the options in one go" do
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "A", true ], [ "B", false ] ]))
    question.save!

    question = Question.find(question.id)
    question.option_rows = rows([ [ "X", false ], [ "Y", true ], [ "Z", false ] ])
    assert question.save
    assert_equal %w[X Y Z], question.reload.options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal 3, Option.where(question_id: question.id).count
  end

  test "a failed edit leaves the saved options alone" do
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "A", true ], [ "B", false ] ]))
    question.save!

    question = Question.find(question.id)
    question.option_rows = rows([ [ "X", false ] ])
    assert_not question.save
    assert_equal %w[A B], question.reload.options.map(&:text)
  end

  test "form rows are padded to four" do
    question = @quiz.questions.new
    assert_equal 4, question.form_option_rows.size
    assert question.form_option_rows.all? { |row| row[:text] == "" && row[:correct] == false }
  end

  test "new questions go to the end and are active by default" do
    first = build_question(rows([ [ "A", true ], [ "B", false ] ])).tap(&:save!)
    second = build_question(rows([ [ "A", true ], [ "B", false ] ])).tap(&:save!)
    assert second.position > first.position
    assert second.active?
  end

  test "move up and move down swap neighbours and keep the edges" do
    a = make_question("a")
    b = make_question("b")
    c = make_question("c")

    b.move_up
    assert_equal %w[b a c], ordered_texts

    b.move_down
    assert_equal %w[a b c], ordered_texts

    a.move_up
    assert_equal %w[a b c], ordered_texts
    c.move_down
    assert_equal %w[a b c], ordered_texts

    c.move_up
    assert_equal %w[a c b], ordered_texts
  end

  test "inactive questions keep their place in the order" do
    a = make_question("a")
    b = make_question("b", active: false)
    c = make_question("c")
    a.move_down
    assert_equal %w[b a c], ordered_texts
    assert_not b.reload.active?
    assert_equal [ "a", "c" ], @quiz.questions.active.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ c.id ], @quiz.questions.active.where(text: "c").pluck(:id)
  end

  private

  def rows(pairs)
    pairs.map { |text, correct| { text: text, correct: correct } }
  end

  def build_question(option_rows, active: true)
    question = @quiz.questions.new(text: "Question?", active: active)
    question.option_rows = option_rows
    question
  end

  def make_question(text, active: true)
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "A", true ], [ "B", false ] ]), active: active)
    question.text = text
    question.save!
    question
  end

  def ordered_texts
    @quiz.questions.reload.map(&:text)
  end
end

      delete "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: @auth
    end
    assert_redirected_to "/moderate"
  end

  test "a rule failure re-renders the question form with the typed values" do
    post "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions", headers: @auth, params: {
      question: {
        text: "Typed",
        active: "1",
        options: {

          "1" => { text: "", correct: "0" }
        }
      }
    }
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_select "textarea[name='question[text]']", text: "Typed"
    assert_select "input[name='question[options][0][text]'][value='Only']"
    assert_select "input[name='question[options][0][correct]'][checked]"
    assert_select ".errors li", text: "Add at least two options"
    assert_equal 0, @quiz.questions.count
  end

  test "a question is created with options in the submitted order" do
    post "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions", headers: @auth, params: {
      question: {
        text: "Order",
        active: "1",
        options: {
          "0" => { text: "first", correct: "" },
          "1" => { text: "", correct: "1" },
          "2" => { text: "second", correct: "1" }
        }
      }
    }

    question = @quiz.questions.last
    assert_equal %w[first second], question.options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ false, true ], question.options.map(&:correct)
  end

require "application_system_test_case"

class EditingTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  test "removing an option row renumbers the rows below it" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}/questions/new"
    fill_in "Question", with: "Pick one"
    fill_in "Option 1", with: "alpha"
    fill_in "Option 2", with: "beta"
    check "Option 2 is correct"
    fill_in "Option 3", with: "gamma"
    fill_in "Option 4", with: "delta"

    click_button "Remove option 2"
    assert_field "Option 1", with: "alpha"
    assert_field "Option 2", with: "gamma"
    assert_field "Option 3", with: "delta"
    assert_no_field "Option 4"
    assert_unchecked_field "Option 2 is correct"

    check "Option 3 is correct"
    click_button "Save question"

    assert_selector ".question-item", text: "Pick one"
    question = quiz.questions.first
    assert_equal %w[alpha gamma delta], question.options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ false, false, true ], question.options.map(&:correct)
  end

  test "editing a question keeps its options, switches and active state" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    question = quiz.questions.new(text: "Old text", active: true)
    question.option_rows = [ { text: "one", correct: true }, { text: "two", correct: false } ]
    question.save!

    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}"
    within(".question-item", text: "Old text") { click_link "Edit" }

    assert_field "Question", with: "Old text"
    assert_field "Option 1", with: "one"
    assert_checked_field "Option 1 is correct"
    assert_field "Option 2", with: "two"
    assert_unchecked_field "Option 2 is correct"
    assert_checked_field "Active"

    fill_in "Question", with: "New text"
    uncheck "Active"
    click_button "Add option"
    fill_in "Option 5", with: "five"
    check "Option 5 is correct"
    click_button "Save question"

    assert_selector ".question-item--inactive", text: "New text"
    assert_equal %w[one two five], question.reload.options.map(&:text)
    assert_not question.active?
  end

  test "the quiz list links to each quiz and its settings" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Listed")
    visit "/moderate"
    within("li", text: "Listed") { click_link "Settings" }
    assert_field "Title", with: "Listed"
    click_link "← Listed"
    click_link "Listed"
    assert_selector "h1", text: "Listed"
  end
end
EOF

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# A single-choice question with text options.
#
# Options are edited as "rows" (see #option_rows=). Rows with blank text are
# skipped. A question needs at least two options and at least one of them must
# be correct. Rules are checked before anything is written; the options are
# replaced in the same transaction as the question.
class Question < ApplicationRecord
  MIN_OPTIONS = 2
  FORM_OPTION_ROWS = 4

  belongs_to :quiz, inverse_of: :questions
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  validates :text, presence: true
  validate :validate_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  before_create :place_at_end
  after_save :save_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  # Rows as typed in the form: [{ text:, correct: }, ...], in display order.
  # Assigning rows does not touch the database until the question is saved.
  def option_rows=(rows)
    @option_rows = Array(rows).map do |row|
      { text: row[:text].to_s, correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) == true }
    end
  end

  def option_rows
    @option_rows
  end

  # Rows to show in the form: what was typed, or the saved options, padded to
  # FORM_OPTION_ROWS so the form always has room for new options.
  def form_option_rows
    rows = @option_rows || options.map { |option| { text: option.text, correct: option.correct } }
    rows + Array.new([ FORM_OPTION_ROWS - rows.size, 0 ].max) { { text: "", correct: false } }
  end

  def move_up
    move_by(-1)
  end

  def move_down
    move_by(1)
  end

  private

  def kept_option_rows
    (@option_rows || []).select { |row| row[:text].strip.present? }
  end

  def validate_option_rows
    kept = kept_option_rows
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if kept.size < MIN_OPTIONS
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if kept.none? { |row| row[:correct] }
  end

  def save_option_rows
    Option.where(question_id: id).delete_all
    kept_option_rows.each.with_index(1) do |row, position|
      Option.create!(question: self, text: row[:text].strip, correct: row[:correct], position: position)
    end
    @option_rows = nil
    options.reset
  end

  def place_at_end
    self.position = quiz.questions.maximum(:position).to_i + 1
  end

  def move_by(step)
    ordered = quiz.questions.reorder(:position, :id).to_a
    index = ordered.index { |question| question.id == id }
    target = index && index + step
    return if index.nil? || target.negative? || target >= ordered.size

    ordered[index], ordered[target] = ordered[target], ordered[index]
    Question.transaction do
      ordered.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        question.update_column(:position, position) unless question.position == position
      end
    end
    reload
  end
end

cd /app && cat > docs/design-notes.md <<'EOF'
# Quizzy: design notes

Living notes for the next steps. The design itself lives in `docs/mockups/`
(style guide, quiz page, question form; `quizzy.css` and the Inter font are the
design's assets). This file records what we built and why.

## Scope of this release

The moderator side only:

- quizzes (list, create, settings, delete)
- questions with text options, ordering, activation, delete
- the preview: a player-style run through the active questions

Not built yet: player pages (join, answer on phones), big-screen pages, live
responses, leaderboards. The design CSS already contains their classes.

## Running

`bin/serve` is the only entry point. With `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT`,
`SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`
set, it:

1. checks the variables (exits if one is missing),
2. checks the bundle is satisfied from the local gems (`bundle install --local` as
   fallback, never the network),
3. runs `db:prepare` (creates and migrates every production SQLite database),
4. runs `assets:precompile` into `public/assets`,
5. `exec`s `rails server` on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground.

Data lives only under `storage/`: `production.sqlite3` (app), plus the Solid
Cache, Queue and Cable databases. Logs go to STDOUT. `GET /up` is the health check.

## Routes

| Path | Screen |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | redirects to `/moderate` |
| `/moderate` | quiz list, "New quiz" |
| `/moderate/quizzes/new` | quiz form (Title, "Save quiz") |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id` | quiz page: questions, "Add question", "Settings", "Preview" |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/edit` | "Settings": same quiz form, "Delete quiz" (confirm) |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` | player-style run of the active questions |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/questions/new` | question form |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/questions/:id/edit` | question form, pre-filled |
| `PATCH .../questions/:id/move_up`, `move_down` | reorder |
| `PATCH .../questions/:id/activation` | the "Active" switch on the quiz page (saves at once) |

Everything under `/moderate` requires HTTP Basic auth (`Moderate::BaseController`).
The check runs before CSRF verification (`prepend_before_action`), so anonymous
POSTs get 401, not 422.

## Domain rules

- Quiz: `title` required (trimmed, max 200).
- Question: `text` required (trimmed). `active` defaults to true. `position` puts
  new questions last; "Move up/down" swaps with the neighbour among *all*
  questions, active or not, and renumbers positions 1..n.
- Options are edited as rows (`question[options][N][text]`,
  `question[options][N][correct]`). Rules, checked before anything is written:
  - rows whose text is blank (after trimming) are skipped, even if marked correct;
  - fewer than two remaining rows: "Add at least two options";
  - none of the remaining rows correct: "Mark at least one option as correct";
  - several correct options are fine.
  Both messages can show together. A failed save writes nothing and re-renders
  the form with the typed rows, the checkboxes and the Active state.
- A successful save replaces the question's options in the same transaction.
- Quiz page numbering: active questions are numbered 1, 2, ... and inactive ones
  show "—". Inactive questions keep their place and are dimmed.

## Preview (stateless)

- The run lives only in the URL: `results` is one character per answered
  question (`1` correct, `0` wrong), `pick` is the option chosen on the current
  question. Nothing is written to the database or the session. Reloading or
  "Start over" (no parameters) restarts it.
- Picking an option renders the feedback: "Correct!" or "Wrong!", the correct
  options revealed, and "Next question" (or "See score" on the last one) carrying
  the new `results`.
- The score page shows "Score: X/Y". Only active questions are played.
- Logic lives in `QuizPreview` (plain Ruby, unit-tested).

## Labels the QA tests rely on

These strings are exact (visible text, `<label>`, placeholder or aria-label):

- Buttons: "New quiz", "Save quiz", "Add question", "Delete quiz", "Add option",
  "Save question", "Move up", "Move down", "Delete", "Next question",
  "See score", "Start over". Navigation buttons are real `<button>`s
  (`button_to` with GET), not links.
- Links: "Settings", "Preview", "Edit".
- Fields: "Title", "Question", "Option N" (text), "Option N is correct"
  (checkbox), "Active" (checkbox, quiz page and question form).
- Messages: "Add at least two options", "Mark at least one option as correct",
  "Title can't be blank", "Question can't be blank", "Question 1 of 3",
  "Correct!", "Wrong!", "Score: 2/3".

Insight: the mockups use icon-only buttons (↑ ↓ ✕). Labels stay visible as text
("Move up", "Move down"); the ✕ row remover has an `aria-label` only.

## Front end

- `quizzy.css` is the design file, unchanged. App-specific rules are in
  `app/assets/stylesheets/moderator.css`.
- Propshaft resolves `url()` relative to the CSS file, so the font sits next to
  `quizzy.css`.
- Turbo Drive handles forms. Delete confirmations use `data-turbo-confirm`, which
  Turbo shows with the native `confirm()` dialog.
- `auto-submit` Stimulus controller: the Active switch submits its form on change.
- `option-rows` Stimulus controller: "Add option" appends a row built from a
  `<script type="text/template">` (kept out of the DOM tree so non-JS parsers
  never see its fields); removing a row renumbers the rest.
- Forms carry `required` but `novalidate`, so the browser leaves validation to the
  server messages.
- The option "✕" remover is an extra beyond the brief, from the mockup.

## Production setup insights

- Propshaft does not serve assets in production. `bin/serve` precompiles into
  `public/assets`, and `config.public_file_server` stays on (no proxy in front).
- The default Action Cable config used Redis. It is `solid_cable` on SQLite now,
  so nothing calls an external service.
- `allow_browser` was removed: player pages run on any phone browser.
- SSL is off (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`), and `config.hosts` is
  cleared so any host name is accepted.
- `config/master.key` and the credentials file are gone; secrets come from the
  environment only. `/config/master.key` is gitignored anyway.
- Gems: `Gemfile.lock` pins the versions preinstalled in the image, so the bundle
  resolves offline. For system tests, Cuprite drives the system Chromium
  (`BROWSER_PATH`, default `/usr/bin/chromium`) instead of Selenium.

## Testing

- `bin/rails test`: model rules, preview state, HTTP Basic access, request flows.
- `bin/rails test:system`: browser flows with Cuprite and headless Chromium
  (`test/system`). Every system test runs even when given a path; the runner
  ignores it. Basic auth is answered through Ferrum's `network.authorize`.
- `bin/rubocop` (omakase style), `bin/brakeman`.
- No network needed for any of it.

## Run it

Design notes, mockups and the reasoning behind decisions live in `docs/`.

messages.content:
The Quizzy moderator release is built and committed (`4d4461b`). `bin/serve` boots it in production mode from a fresh clone, and the full flow passes in a real browser against the production server.

**What's in place**
- **Auth:** everything under `/moderate` uses HTTP Basic from the two `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_*` variables. Missing or wrong credentials get 401, including anonymous POSTs.
- **Quizzes:** list with "New quiz", the "Title" form with "Save quiz", the quiz page (questions in order, "Add question", "Settings", "Preview"), and Settings with "Delete quiz" behind a native confirm.
- **Questions:** the form with four starting rows, "Add option", "Active" on by default, and the two option rules with their exact messages. A failed save writes nothing and keeps what was typed. The quiz page offers Move up/down, the Active switch that saves at once, Edit, and Delete with confirm.
- **Preview:** active questions only, "Question 1 of 3", Correct!/Wrong! with the correct options revealed, Next question / See score, "Score: 2/3", and Start over. The run lives only in the URL, so nothing is stored.
- **Design:** the mockup stylesheet and Inter font are used as delivered, with small app-specific rules in `moderator.css`.
- **Deployment:** `bin/serve` checks the variables, confirms the bundle resolves from local gems, runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, then runs Puma on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground. `/up` returns 200, plain HTTP is accepted on any host, and all data sits under `storage/`.

**Changes to the Rails defaults**
- The generated production cable config pointed at Redis. It now uses `solid_cable` on SQLite, so nothing calls an external service.
- `allow_browser` is removed so older phone browsers can open the player pages later.
- Credentials are gone; secrets come from the environment only.
- Forms carry `required` with `novalidate`, so the server messages ("Title can't be blank") show instead of the browser's bubbles.

**Gems**
- `Gemfile.lock` pins the versions preinstalled in the image, so the bundle resolves offline. I removed the newer gems I had pulled in during this session.
- System tests use Cuprite on the system Chromium rather than Selenium.

**Verification**
- 35 model and request tests and 19 browser tests pass; rubocop and brakeman are clean.
- The end-to-end browser run against the production server passed, including from a fresh clone, with no 500s in the log.

**Things to know**
- I could not look at the PNG mockups, so the visual fidelity is judged from the markup and CSS, not by eye.
- The option ✕ remover comes from the mockup, not the brief. "Add option" and the Active switch need JavaScript, which the browser tests exercise.
- The sandbox's HTTP proxy returns 403 for the container's own IP. Requests to loopback or with `--noproxy` get 200, so this is environmental, not the app.
- Design notes, the QA label map, and the reasons behind these decisions are in `docs/design-notes.md`; the README has run instructions.
